worldview.title: 1 · Worldview
worldview.intro: Three paths: A real-world backdrop (only write custom deviations), B small world (iterate complete), C big world (split into a constant core plus triggered detail). Constant entries burn tokens in every prompt; triggered ones light up on keywords.
worldview.placeholder: Path C. A harbor town under thirty years of fog; bells carry news; the lighthouse lights only half its lamp (keeper secret)…
worldview.q1: Which path fits this card: A real backdrop, B small world, or C big world?
worldview.q2: What is ALWAYS true here that a model would guess wrong? (that is your constant core)
worldview.q3: Which places, factions or names deserve their own triggered entry, under which keywords?

basics.title: 2 · Character basics
basics.intro: The differentiation principle: write ONLY what deviates from the model's default assumption. “A Japanese girl with black hair” says nothing — blonde dye, a scar, a wrong accent make the cut.
basics.placeholder: Ali, deckhand, 24. Scar from left brow to cheekbone — her smile pulls sideways. Speaks in dock shorthand…
basics.q1: Name, rough age, occupation or identity?
basics.q2: Which traits DEVIATE from what a model would assume by default? Only those are worth ink.
basics.q3: What would a stranger notice within three seconds (scar, gait, accent, habit)?
basics.q4: Which single background fact drives how they act today?

palette.title: 3 · Personality palette
palette.intro: A base coat under everything, 1-2 main colors people actually see, one accent as seasoning. Every main color needs handwritten derivation loops — scene → behavior → spoken line. Illogical-but-alive combinations are what only a person can write.
palette.placeholder: Base: inferiority (never speaks first). Main: competitive (loses, then drills all night claiming it's “just exercise”)…
palette.q1: The base coat — the trait lying under everything?
palette.q2: The 1-2 main colors people actually see day to day?
palette.q3: One small accent trait as seasoning?
palette.q4: For EACH main color, handwrite derivation loops: a concrete scene → what they do → one spoken line.

facets.title: 4 · Three facets (optional)
facets.intro: Gears of ONE engine, not three personalities. Each facet = trigger + energy + voice + body + function, and the other facets bleed through it. Skip this for simple characters.
facets.placeholder: Day-shift deckhand (strangers present): short sentences, hands never idle. Night watcher (alone on the pier): …
facets.q1: What flips the character between facets — place, audience, threat?
facets.q2: For each facet: what energy runs it, and what does the voice sound like (give a sample line)?
facets.q3: What does each facet DO for them — its function?
facets.q4: How do the other facets bleed through each one?

exegesis.title: 5 · Second exegesis
exegesis.intro: The author's final margin notes — what stops the model from completing your character out of its own training data. Entirely handwritten; the AI may only ask you questions.
exegesis.placeholder: She is NOT a tsundere template: her sharp tongue targets only the strong; with the weak she is plainly direct. Never write her blushing.
exegesis.q1: What is this character NOT — which obvious reading is wrong?
exegesis.q2: What would a model wrongly auto-complete from its stock tropes?
exegesis.q3: What stays fixed no matter where the story goes?

wardrobe.title: 6 · Wardrobe & carried items
wardrobe.intro: Triggered-layer entries keyed on outfit words and the character's name. Every item should hold a story — a lighter that no longer lights beats a catalog of clothes.
wardrobe.placeholder: Work jacket, cuffs frayed, a knife sheath sewn into the left pocket. Carries her mother's cracked compass…
wardrobe.q1: Daily outfit — and the one detail that is off or wrong about it?
wardrobe.q2: What do they always carry, and what story does each item hold?
wardrobe.q3: Which keywords should trigger these entries?

nsfw.title: 7 · NSFW palette (optional)
nsfw.intro: Write the WHY, not the WHAT: drives, dynamics and boundaries as personality facts. The core motivation is handwritten-only. Entries land keeper-only. What you write is organized faithfully — no watering down.
nsfw.placeholder: Intimacy is the only way she ever goes off-watch — that is the why…
nsfw.q1: WHY does intimacy matter to this character — what does it mean to them? (handwritten)
nsfw.q2: Which dynamics and preferences follow from their personality, stated as facts?

npcs.title: 8 · NPCs
npcs.intro: One triggered entry per NPC, keyed on the name. One concrete, memorable detail each — an NPC exists to be recognized, not summarized.
npcs.placeholder: Old Chen, foreman, owes her his life and keeps trying to repay it in fish…
npcs.q1: Who orbits this character — two to four people at most?
npcs.q2: One concrete distinguishing detail per NPC?
npcs.q3: Which keywords trigger each entry (usually the name)?

overview.title: 9 · Quick reference
overview.intro: The always-on index card: 8-15 terse lines the model must never lose sight of. It rides in every prompt — every line must earn its tokens.
overview.placeholder: Ali / deckhand / scar brow→cheek / base: inferiority, main: competitive / investigating the lighthouse night…
overview.q1: Which 8-15 lines must the model never lose sight of?
overview.q2: What is the current situation as the story opens?

opening.title: 10 · Opening message
opening.intro: The opening sets the register the model will imitate. Place the player, give the character one concrete action and real dialogue, end on a hook. The anti-pattern lint applies at full force.
opening.placeholder: The bell struck four. Ali looped the mooring line without looking up: “You're standing where a man died last night.”
opening.q1: Where does the scene open, and what is the character DOING?
opening.q2: What is their first spoken line?
opening.q3: What hook can the player immediately act on?

variables.title: 11 · Variables & state
variables.intro: Loreweaver-native closing stage: [InitVar] YAML for initial state — scalar leaves auto-promote to typed, validated variables — plus plain-language update rules that land as a hooks draft.
variables.placeholder: Trust 0..10 starting 0; lighthouse clues 0..5; has-seen-the-fog flag…
variables.q1: Which state does the STORY actually read back — meters, stages, flags?
variables.q2: Ranges and starting values for each?
variables.q3: When does each variable move, and by how much (one rule per line)?
